target_customer: Corporate government affairs teams and businesses exposed to legislation
problem: Tracking thousands of federal and state bills and responding with amendments is slow and costly with incumbent tools and lobbyists.
product_category: AI legislative monitoring and government affairs agents

founders.name: Winston Wei
education: Williams College, CS and American Studies

competitors.name: Quorum
competitors.what: Legislative tracking and government affairs platform

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting bills from Congress and 50 states and drafting amendments with LLMs is standard engineering with hard accuracy parts.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbents hold data and relationships; a legislator relationship graph is the potential moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features in 2026 (such as an MCP server); no action against Fed10 found.

market_need_then: Sources report thousands of relevant bills introduced between 2023 and 2026 and rising AI lobbying activity in Washington.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct; positioned for 'ambitious government affairs teams', YC listing says 'AI Lobbyists'

branding.brand_signature: Founders' record of passing a Nevada bill (AB367) before voting age

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable founder story but the name 'Fed10' may suggest federal only and evidence of brand pull is thin.

outcome_analysis: Fed10 is a Winter 2026 YC company founded by three people with legislative experience who helped pass a Nevada bill. It sells AI legislative monitoring against Quorum, FiscalNote and Bloomberg. No funding or outcome is verified, so its trajectory depends on winning enterprise distribution from entrenched incumbents.
notes: YC page lists schools but a launch post says founders dropped out; conflict unresolved. VCBacked says $500K pre-seed announced March 2026 and another profile says $130K seed; aggregators only, not recorded. Founder technical flags follow YC page roles. 'Built by ex-lobbyists' is company claim.
